newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Golds guide Australian stocks to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Golds guide Australian stocks to higher close.

text.p: A polished performance from the gold sector led the Australian share market to a stronger close on Tuesday, although gains were trimmed in the afternoon.
The All Ordinaries index rose 8.1 points to 2,731.9 after peaking in the first half hour of trade at 2,741.3.
Brokers said business was at moderate levels with light gains in some of the leaders enough to overcome afternoon profit-taking in key miners BHP and WMC.
BHP closed 11 cents lower at A$18.22 after peaking at A$18.54 (US$13.72), while WMC ended steady at A$7.87 after hitting a high of A$8.04.
"BHP and WMC got pegged back but the business was nothing exceptional," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.
Golds posted the biggest gains, the sector index holding near its highs for most of the day to add 2.6 percent, compared to a gain in the broader market of just 0.3 percent.
Normandy Mining, making up about 23 percent of the gold index, climbed 2.6 percent to A$1.59, while Acacia Resources jumped 2.8 percent to A$1.48.

Great Central Mining added 4.7 percent to A$2.65. Newcrest Mining also shone, climbing 5.7 percent to A$2.80, aided by forecasts of production at its Gosowong project and after news of a return to profit for its Telfer mine in Western Australia.
"Golds were the standout. The rest were neither here nor there," the dealer said.
Elsewhere, share registry services group Computershare climbed 20 cents to A$12.20 after announcing the purchase of two registry units from accounting giants Ernst and Young and KPMG.
Australis Media added 2.5 cents to 21 cents after reinstatement to trading after news of its pay TV deal.

The deal would see rival operator Foxtel, owned by News Corp and government-owned telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp, taking a controlling stake in Australis. The deal remains subject to due diligence and regulatory approvals.
News Corp shares closed 10 cents higher at A$6.33, helped by a strong showing from its ADRs in New York trading.
Alan Jackon's Austrim Ltd jumped 42 cents to A$4.60 after Monday's sharp rise in annual profit to A$21.9 million and the setting of a 2-for-5 rights issue.
Traders said the market appeared well supported around current levels with hopes for an interest rate cut still uppermost in most investors' minds.
"A lot of people are just sitting on their hands until they see what the Reserve Bank is going to do with interest rates," said Wilson HTM broker Scott Healey.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about of seven to five. About 27 perent of stocks traded were steady.
